Internals npmatch's matching code calls

Source: R/for-npmatch.R
np_tokenize.Rd

Thin, exported wrappers around four internal helpers, so npmatch's blocking, comparison and geography code can call them without reaching into this package's internals. Most users never call these.

Usage

np_tokenize(frame, token_col, stopwords, min_token_len, concat_adjacent)

np_doc_freq(row, token)

np_addr_key(street_keys, zip5 = NULL)

np_state_abb(state)

Arguments

frame

A data frame holding token_col.

token_col

The column to tokenize.

stopwords

Tokens to drop (see np_stopwords()).

min_token_len

Shortest token kept.

concat_adjacent

Also index adjacent-token concatenations.

row, token

Parallel vectors: the row each token came from, and the token.

street_keys, zip5

Street keys and ZIP codes from np_normalize().

state

State names or codes.

Value

np_tokenize(): a list of base and concatenated token tables. np_doc_freq(): a named numeric vector of row counts per token. np_addr_key(): a character vector of address keys. np_state_abb(): a character vector of two-letter codes, NA where none applies.

Details

  • np_tokenize() splits a column into tokens for the blocking index, as npmatch::np_ref_index() and npmatch::np_block() do.

  • np_doc_freq() counts, for each token, the rows it appears in.

  • np_addr_key() builds the address key np_addr_freq() counts on: the street key and ZIP, blank for a PO box.

  • np_state_abb() maps a state name or code to its two-letter code.

They are not part of the normalizer signature: each calls a function that is (np_normalize_signature()), and adds nothing of its own.
